en: And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it to us, Abu Mu'awiyah and Waki' narrated to us; (H) and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us; (H) and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Khalid—meaning al-Ahmar—narrated to us, all of them from al-A'mash, with this chain of transmission, the like of it.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, they said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from Masruq, he said: We entered upon 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr when Mu'awiyah came to Kufa. He mentioned the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "He was neither obscene in speech nor did he deliberately utter obscenities." And he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, among the best of you are those of you with the best character." 'Uthman said: "when he arrived with Mu'awiyah at Kufa."

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah: he heard 'Abdullah ibn Abi 'Utbah narrating from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri; (H) and Zuhayr ibn Harb, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us—Zuhayr said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, he said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn Abi 'Utbah saying: I heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was more modest than a virgin in her private chamber; and whenever he disliked something, we would recognize it in his face.

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Waki' and 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Qays, from Jarir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace); (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi 'Umar, and Ahmad ibn 'Abdah narrated to us, they said: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr, from Jarir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of the hadith of al-A'mash.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, both from Jarir; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and 'Ali ibn Khashram narrated to us, they said: 'Isa ibn Yunus informed us; (H) and Abu Kurayb, Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (H) and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Hafs—meaning Ibn Ghiyath—narrated to us, all of them from al-A'mash, from Zayd ibn Wahb and Abu Zibyan, from Jarir ibn 'Abdullah, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever does not show mercy to people, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not show mercy to him."

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri: Abu Salamah narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) the like of it.

'Amr al-Naqid and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to me, both from Sufyan; 'Amr said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that al-Aqra' ibn Habis saw the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) kissing al-Hasan, so he said: "Indeed, I have ten children, and I have never kissed a single one of them." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, they said: Abu Usamah and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from 'A'ishah, she said: Some Bedouin people came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "Do you kiss your children?" They said: "Yes." They said: "But by Allah, we do not kiss them." The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Can I help it if Allah has stripped mercy from you?" And Ibn Numayr said: "mercy from your heart?"

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr's—they said: Isma'il—who is Ibn 'Ulayyah—narrated to us, from Ayyub, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Anas ibn Malik, he said: I never saw anyone more merciful toward family and children than the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). He said: Ibrahim was being nursed in the upper suburbs of Medina; he would go there, accompanied by us, and enter the house—which was filled with smoke, as his foster-father was a blacksmith—and he would take him and kiss him, and then return. 'Amr said: When Ibrahim passed away, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, Ibrahim is my son, and he died while still suckling, and he has two wet nurses who will complete his suckling in Paradise."

Haddab ibn Khalid and Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us, both from Sulayman—and the wording is Shayban's—Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "A boy was born to me tonight, and I have named him after the name of my forefather Ibrahim." Then he handed him over to Umm Sayf, the wife of a blacksmith named Abu Sayf. He set out to visit him, and I followed him. We reached Abu Sayf while he was blowing his bellows, and the house had filled with smoke. I quickened my pace ahead of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Abu Sayf, hold on! The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) has arrived." So he stopped, and the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) called for the child, held him close to himself, and said whatever Allah willed him to say. Anas said: I later saw him breathing his last in the arms of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). The eyes of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) shed tears, and he said: "The eye weeps, and the heart grieves, but we do not say anything except what pleases our Lord; and by Allah, O Ibrahim, we are indeed sorrowful over your departure."

Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Maymun narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us: 'Amr ibn Dinar informed me, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah; and he said: Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir informed me, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, he said: When the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) died, wealth came to Abu Bakr from al-'Ala' ibn al-Hadrami, so Abu Bakr said: "Whoever was owed a debt by the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) or was given a promise by him, let him come to us"... similar to the hadith of Ibn 'Uyaynah.

'Amr al-Naqid narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir, that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah; (H) and Ishaq narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, from Ibn al-Munkadir from Jabir, and from 'Amr from Muhammad ibn 'Ali from Jabir, one of them adding to the other; (H) and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us—and the wording is his—he said: Sufyan said: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir saying: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah; and Sufyan said: I also heard 'Amr ibn Dinar narrating from Muhammad ibn 'Ali, who said: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, and one of them added to the other, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "If the wealth of Bahrain were to come to us, I would give you like this, like this, and like this"—gesturing with both of his hands. But the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed away before the wealth of Bahrain arrived. When it was brought to Abu Bakr afterwards, he ordered a caller who announced: "Whoever was promised something by the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) or was owed a debt, let him come." So I stood up and said: "Indeed, the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: If the wealth of Bahrain were to come to us, I would give you like this, like this, and like this." So Abu Bakr scooped up a handful once, and then said to me: "Count it." I counted it, and behold, it was five hundred. He said: "Take twice as much again."

Abu al-Tahir, Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Sarh narrated to me, 'Abdullah ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) led the expedition of the Conquest—the Conquest of Mecca—then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) marched out with those of the Muslims who were with him, and they fought at Hunayn. Allah granted victory to His religion and the Muslims, and on that day the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) gave Safwan ibn Umayyah one hundred camels, then one hundred, then one hundred. Ibn Shihab said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me that Safwan said: "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) gave me what he gave me while he was the most hated of people to me, and he continued giving to me until he became the most beloved of people to me."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas, that a man asked the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) for sheep filling the valley between two mountains, so he gave them to him. The man then returned to his people and said: "O my people, embrace Islam! For by Allah, Muhammad gives such a gift as if he fears no poverty." Anas said: A man might embrace Islam desiring nothing but worldly gain, but he would not stay Muslim long before Islam became dearer to him than the worldly life and all that is in it.

'Asim ibn al-Nadr al-Taymi narrated to us, Khalid—meaning Ibn al-Harith—narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, from Musa ibn Anas, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was never asked for anything for the sake of Islam except that he gave it. He said: A man came to him, so he gave him sheep filling the valley between two mountains. The man returned to his people and said: "O my people, embrace Islam! For indeed Muhammad gives such a gift as one who fears no destitution."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, al-Ashja'i narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, 'Abd al-Rahman—meaning Ibn Mahdi—narrated to us, both from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, he said: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah saying the exact same thing.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and 'Amr al-Naqid narrated to us, they said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir: he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah say: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was never asked for anything at all and said "No."

Shayban ibn Farrukh and Abu al-Rabi' narrated to us, they said: 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, from Anas ibn Malik, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had the finest character among all people.

Abu Ma'n al-Raqashi, Zayd ibn Yazid narrated to me, 'Umar ibn Yunus informed us, 'Ikrimah—who is Ibn 'Ammar—narrated to us, he said: Ishaq said: Anas said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was of the best character among people. One day he sent me for an errand, so I said: "By Allah, I will not go," while in my heart I intended to go to do what the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) commanded me. So I went out until I passed by some boys playing in the marketplace. Suddenly the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) took hold of the nape of my neck from behind. He said: I looked at him and he was laughing, and he said: "O Unays, did you go where I ordered you?" I said: "Yes, I am going, O Messenger of Allah." Anas said: By Allah, I served him for nine years, and I never knew him to say regarding anything I did, "Why did you do such and such?" or regarding anything I left undone, "Why did you not do such and such?"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Zakariyya narrated to us, Sa'id—who is Ibn Abi Burdah—narrated to me, from Anas, he said: I served the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) for nine years, and I never knew him to say to me at all, "Why did you do such and such?" nor did he ever criticize me for anything.

And Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Zuhayr ibn Harb both narrated it to us from Isma'il—and the wording is Ahmad's—they said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, from Anas, he said: When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) arrived in Medina, Abu Talhah took me by the hand and went with me to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), saying: "O Messenger of Allah, Anas is an intelligent boy, so let him serve you." He said: So I served him while traveling and while resident; by Allah, he never said to me regarding anything I did, "Why did you do this in such a way?" nor regarding anything I did not do, "Why did you not do this in such a way?"
And Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated it to us, Sallam ibn Miskin narrated to us, Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from Anas, the like of it.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Abu al-Rabi' narrated to us, they said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, he said: I served the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) for ten years. By Allah, he never said "Uff" to me at all, nor did he ever say to me regarding anything, "Why did you do such and such?" or "Why didn't you do such and such?" Abu al-Rabi' added: "regarding what a servant does," and did not mention his words: "By Allah."

And Abu Kurayb narrated it to us, Ibn Mubarak narrated to us, from Yunus; (H) and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, both from al-Zuhri, with this chain of transmission, similar to it.

Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim narrated to us, Ibrahim—meaning Ibn Sa'd—narrated to us, from al-Zuhri; (H) and Abu 'Imran, Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Ziyad narrated to me—and the wording is his—Ibrahim informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was the most generous of people in doing good, and he was at his most generous during the month of Ramadan. Indeed, Jibril (peace be upon him) used to meet him every year in Ramadan until it drew to an end, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) would recite the Quran to him. When Jibril met him, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was more generous in giving good than the blowing wind.

And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated it to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us; (H) and Yahya ibn Habib narrated it to me, Khalid—meaning Ibn al-Harith—narrated to us, both said: Shu'bah narrated to us, with this chain of transmission. And in the hadith of Ibn Ja'far, he said: "a horse belonging to us," and did not say: "belonging to Abu Talhah." And in the hadith of Khalid from Qatadah: "I heard Anas."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from Anas, he said: There was an alarm in Medina, so the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) borrowed a horse belonging to Abu Talhah called Mandub and rode it. He then said: "We saw no cause for alarm, and indeed we found it as swift as a sea."

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki, and Abu Kamil narrated to us—and the wording is Yahya's; Yahya said: informed us, and the others said: narrated to us—Hammad ibn Zayd, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was the best of people, the most generous of people, and the bravest of people. One night the people of Medina were alarmed, so some people went out toward the sound. They were met by the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) returning, having already preceded them to the sound. He was riding a bareback horse belonging to Abu Talhah with a sword hung around his neck, saying: "Do not be alarmed, do not be alarmed!" He said: "We found it as swift as a sea," or "Indeed, it is a sea." He said: And it was a horse that used to be considered slow.

Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to me, 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith informed us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, Sa'd narrated to us, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, he said: On the day of Uhud, I saw on the right of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and on his left two men wearing white garments fighting fiercely on his behalf; I had never seen them before nor after.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr and Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Mis'ar, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Sa'd, he said: On the day of Uhud, I saw on the right of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and on his left two men wearing white garments whom I had never seen before nor after—meaning Jibril and Mika'il (peace be upon them both).
